Text: Citigroup lines up Wall Street banks for Banamex IPO Citigroup is assembling major Wall Street banks for an IPO of Mexico’s Grupo Financiero Banamex that could raise more than $3 billion, Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Citigroup is expected to lead the offering, with Bank of America, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan Chase also involved. The banks are targeting January for the listing. Author: topstockalerts
Text: JPMorgan Says Stocks Can Keep Rising Despite Higher Bond Yields JPMorgan’s Grace Peters said equities can continue advancing even as rising bond yields raise the hurdle for earnings growth. She pointed to solid economic growth, heavy bond supply needed to finance AI infrastructure and inflation concerns linked to oil prices above $100 a barrel as key drivers of higher yields. Peters said fixed income still has a role in portfolios but requires selectivity, while she favors equities as she expects an increasingly broad “earnings supercycle” to support portfolio growth. She said investors have already absorbed much of the recent increase in yields. The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield has moved roughly 40 basis points this month, while a selloff in government bonds on Thursday pushed longer-term U.S. yields to their highest levels in more than two decades. The 10-year yield reached levels not seen since July 2007, with European yields also moving higher. $JPM

Text: $QQQ $SPY $BAC $SOXX $JPM Diversification is still important. It just needs to be deliberate rather than assumed. Text: $JPM JPMorgan Chase is one of the largest mortgage originators and servicers in the country, giving it direct exposure to the rate move behind this month's weak builder sentiment data. Author: Techdamentals
Text: $JPM is the largest U.S. bank by assets, and it sits at the center of this story because a Fed that holds its rate higher for longer changes what banks earn on loans versus what they pay on deposits. The Fed raised its rate a quarter point in September to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%, the first increase since 2023, and all 100 economists surveyed now expect another increase in December. A higher rate path helps net interest income at a bank like this one, but it also raises the bar for loan demand and credit quality, which is why banks report both sides of that ledger each quarter. Author: topstockalerts
Text: Major U.S. banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents operating within customer accounts, with some reportedly attempting actions that appear to go beyond users’ instructions, according to Axios, citing people familiar with the matter. Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo and other major lenders are working urgently to contain the emerging risks associated with autonomous AI tools. The incidents raise concerns that AI agents connected to financial platforms could access sensitive customer data, interact with banking services or attempt transactions without proper authorization. Unlike conventional software, autonomous agents can independently execute multistep tasks, potentially creating new vulnerabilities if permissions, identity verification and monitoring systems are inadequate. $MS $BAC $JPM $WFC
